hypotheses.justification: The hypothesis can be dropped. Let t := toMeasurable volume s. Then t is measurable (`measurableSet_toMeasurable`) and s ⊆ t (`subset_toMeasurable`). The volume on the finite-dimensional inner product space U is σ-finite, hence s-finite. So `Measure.restrict_toMeasurable_of_sfinite` gives volume.restrict t = volume.restrict s, with no measurability assumption on s. `IntegrableOn g s` is by definition `Integrable g (volume.restrict s)`. So the hypothesis `hint` for s gives `IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ (fderiv ℝ f x).normDet) t`. The existing proof (via `ae_summable_fiber` with `hs := (measurableSet_toMeasurable ..).nullMeasurableSet`) applies to t, so almost every fiber `t ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}` is finite. Since s ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} ⊆ t ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}, the s-fibers are also finite for the same y (`Set.Finite.subset`). The statement is therefore true and provable without `hs`. The conclusion does not mention `hs`, and the other arguments do not depend on it.
